name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret. It’s safe, reversible, and fixes formatting drift without touching logic—no risk of breaking behavior. The trade-off is manual review of edge cases where whitespace changes could affect tooling (like code formatters), but those are rare and detectable.

name: Gauge
text: Risk isn’t just edge cases—whitespace patches to third-party deps can break tooling that parses ASTs (e.g., linters, bundlers) if they rely on exact token positions. Better alternative: auto-apply only to files where the repo’s own CI enforces formatting (e.g., Prettier config), and gate it on a test that checks AST stability post-patch. Settle it by running the patch on a sample of dependencies and verifying no CI failures.
